finding: Published 16 Nov 2026, 22:01 UTC. The comparison event itself. Chase: slow transactions and online banking trouble; outage reports rose from 9 am Eastern, peaked at 4,810 at 2 pm, 2,328 at 4:23 pm. Chase: a technical issue, not a cyberattack. AP, CBS and Bloomberg also named Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Truist, U.S. Bank, Capital One and Zelle from user reports. Zelle: operating as it should. U.S. Bank: not directly affected.
Published 2 Oct 2024. Outside the window (before 11 Nov 2024).
Published 29 Apr 2025. Citibank online and mobile banking inaccessible "earlier today". Duration not stated in the visible text (paywall).
Published 17 Nov 2026. About this week: Chase, with Wells Fargo and Bank of America customers reporting difficulty. No list of earlier outages.

Published 21 Jan 2025. Capital One customers could not get direct deposits, see balances or log in, from Wednesday 15 Jan to Sunday 19 Jan 2025. Vendor FIS blamed a local power loss and hardware failure and said it was not a cyber incident. More than two dozen institutions affected. Citi app trouble the same day; whether connected is unknown.

Published 17 Nov 2026. The comparison event itself. Chase reports began about 10 am Eastern, peaked near 4,700 at 2 pm; transactions normal by Monday evening. Chase on X about 3 pm: "a temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems", no evidence of a cyberattack, other banks affected only where party to a transaction with Chase, "not a systemic issue". Bank of America: systems operating normally. Capital One: no issues. Reports at six other banks peaked between 2 and 3 pm.

Published 15 Jan 2025. Citi mobile app login failing from about 6 am Pacific on 15 Jan; Citi said the app was operational at 5:44 am Pacific on 16 Jan: about 24 hours. Cause: "technical issues". Website offered as the way in. CNBC is cited as reporting on it.
